title: Model slot availability and soft-quota simulation
summary: Quick simulation and playbook for limiting model onboarding impact via a soft-quota slot allocator and prioritized KV eviction. Focus: new model onboarding bursts, KV cache footprint per session, and availability of low-latency slots across regions.
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet documents a lightweight simulation we ran to evaluate model slot availability under a 'soft-quota' allocator for new-model onboards. Instead of rigid reserved capacity we allow ephemeral soft slots that can be throttled/evicted preferentially to protect customer SLOs. Objective is to quantify: 1) how many soft slots we can admit per region without increasing p50/p90 tail above targets, 2) expected incremental KV cache footprint, and 3) recommended soft-quota admission policy knobs.

Background context / why this matters:
- Recent onboarding of a 30B decoder-only model in eu-west led to increased KV reuse and eviction churn; saw a 15% p95 latency bump during first 48h.
- We need an onboarding mode that lets teams validate correctness at scale while limiting impact to production tenants.
- Existing approaches (full reserved capacity or rolling canary) either cost too much or are operationally slow. Soft-quota aims for faster onboarding with measured risk.

Key definitions used in the sim:
- Slot: a schedulable GPU execution context capable of serving model inferences with KV.
- Hard quota: permanently reserved slots for a customer or model.
- Soft quota: ephemeral admission count; can be reclaimed by allocator under pressure and have lower eviction priority.
- Prefetch factor: how many KV pages we pre-warm per session open. Controls warmup traffic and short-lived cache pressure.
- Eviction_priority: integer where lower == evict first. Soft slots marked with priority 100, production slots 10.

Assumptions and inputs (explicit):
- Fleet: eu-west region has 1600 active slots (cumulative across GTX/ A100 pools) during peak.
- Baseline steady-state qps (all models) = 75k requests/min region-wide; sequence length median = 128 tokens.
- New model expected initial qps if unrestricted = 3k req/min after rollout wave (weekend soft-onboard spike).
- Average KV per session = 1.15MB (profiles from model artifact: 9 layers cached at 128-seqlen typical) with prefetch_factor = 2.
- KV cache TTL default = 12h; soft-slot sessions TTL = 1h to limit long-lived footprint unless promoted.
- Allocation reaction time for reclaiming soft slots = 10s (fast reclaim path implemented in scheduler prototype).

Simulation approach (summary):
- Discrete-event sim at 1s granularity for a 6-hour window centered on expected spike.
- Events: new session open (soft or hard), evictions triggered when mem pressure > 90% of region cache capacity, slot reclaim when latency degradation observed.
- Latency cost model: per-request baseline time + additional penalty proportional to KV miss rate and batch fragmentation. Latency penalty observed empirically ~ 2ms per KV miss for medium models, but with tail effects multiplied by 1.8 for concurrent evictions.

Scenarios run:
1) Baseline (no new onboarding): measure current p50/p90/p95.
2) Soft-quota conservative admit: admit up to 200 soft slots with prefetch_factor=1 and KV-TTL=1h.
3) Soft-quota aggressive admit: admit up to 500 soft slots with prefetch_factor=2 and KV-TTL=4h.
4) Promote-throughput scenario: soft slots are promoted to hard if sustained qps>50 req/min per slot for >30m.
5) No-soft (control): rolling canary reserving 150 hard slots.

Key outputs (high-level numbers from sim):
- Baseline p95 latency: 187ms.
- Scenario 2 (conservative soft 200): p95 latency median change +3.2% (to ~193ms). p99 unmodeled but small. Region KV cache increase: +220MB steady; eviction churn +12%. No SLO breaches observed in sim.
- Scenario 3 (aggressive soft 500): p95 latency +11.8% (to ~209ms), p99 shows amplified tail events in simulated traces; KV footprint +620MB, eviction churn +42%, observed short-lived spike in cold miss-rate causing 1.6x backend load for 8min windows.
- Scenario 4 (promote-throughput): similar to scenario 2 initially; promoting 50 slots after 60m caused minor bump but overall safer than scenario 3 because promotion is gated.
- No-soft (control): p95 stable, but cost of reserved 150 hard slots equates to ~2.3x cost of conservative soft approach for equivalent initial capacity.

Interpretation / takeaways:
- A conservative soft admission (<= 200 slots) with prefetch_factor=1 and 1h TTL gives a good balance: negligible latency impact and small KV footprint.
- Aggressive admissions without tighter TTLs quickly saturate region KV memory and produce eviction storms that amplify tail latency. This is the main failure mode.
- Fast reclaim (10s) is necessary but not sufficient; TTL and prefetch behavior matter more to avoid repeated churn.
- Promotion rules (thresholded by sustained QPS) reduce risk by making promoted sessions behave like hard quota only after they've proved value.

Operational playbook (initial proposal):
- Default onboarding posture = conservative soft admission in each region: max_soft_slots = min(200, 12% of active slots) with prefetch_factor=1 and KV_TTL_soft=1h.
- Autoscale safety rail: if region p95 latency increases >6% sustained over 10m, automatically reduce soft quota by 50% and throttle onboarding traffic.
- Monitoring: add a dedicated dashboard tile for 'soft-slot eviction rate' and 'soft-slot KV footprint' with 1m rollups.
- Rollout steps for next model onboarding: 1) internal shadowing on 50 soft slots for 3h, 2) expand to 150 soft slots over 2h, 3) monitor and optionally promote slow cohort.

Short TODOs / open questions:
- Run real-world A/B across two small regions (eu-west / us-central) for the next onboarding to validate sim numbers (owner: Diego).
- Validate KV per session estimate for the 30B family on latest quantized runtime (owner: Hannah).
- Wire alerts: INFRA-9812 to map alert -> autoscaler action (owner: Owen).
- Perf concern: confirm allocator reclaim latency at scale (1000 concurrent reclaims) on staging cluster.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: soft slots could be used by noisy tenants repeatedly causing continual churn. Mitigation: add per-tenant soft-slot fairness caps and cooldown windows.
- Risk: mis-estimated KV footprint for corner-case prompts grows the footprint 3x. Mitigation: conservative prefetch + TTL + emergency drain policy.

Notes on follow-ups and artifacts:
- Attached spreadsheet (TODO): rough sim input table and region capacity model under different fleet mixes. See Confluence page in links.
- Recommend we bake simulation into infra-sim harness and expose knobs as Feature Flags so we can toggle prefetch/ttl per rollout.

Appendix: short sample sim trace excerpt (verbatim):
- t=00:12:43 new soft session 0x7b opened, kv_alloc=1.05MB, slot_alloc=s12
- t=00:12:54 reclaim triggered due to mem>90%: evict soft session 0x3f, reclaim latency spike observed +21ms on 12 requests
- t=01:02:01 promote: session 0x7b promoted after 35m sustained qps=62/min

If you want this converted to a spreadsheet with the per-minute sim series and plotted p95 curves, I can export the raw sim CSV and drop it into the shared 'infra-sims' sheet.

Notes to self: keep names intentionally conservative for first two rollouts; avoid global promotion rules until we have cross-region sim confidence.
